# CC2ASN

> CC2ASN is a free lookup service that returns every AS number (ASN), IPv4 prefix and IPv6 prefix (IP range) registered to a country. Send a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code over HTTPS or whois and get the full list back. The data is rebuilt daily from the delegation statistics files of the five regional internet registries: AFRINIC, APNIC, ARIN, LACNIC and RIPE NCC.

Important: this is registration data, not geolocation. A record shows the country the registry has on file for the holder of a network, not where its addresses are in use today.

## API (HTTPS)

Base URL: `https://api.cc2asn.com/`. Country codes work in upper or lower case. Answers are plain text, one record per line; add `?format=json` for JSON.

- `GET /NO`: every AS number registered to Norway
- `GET /IPV4/NO`: every IPv4 prefix registered to Norway, in CIDR notation
- `GET /IPV6/NO`: every IPv6 prefix registered to Norway
- `GET /ALL/NO`: AS numbers, IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes together
- `GET /ALL/NO?format=json`: the same as JSON

AS numbers come back with the AS prefix (`AS224`), prefixes in CIDR notation (`2.148.0.0/14`). JSON answers have the shape `{"cc": "NO", "type": "ALL", "date": "latest", "records": [...]}`.

Example: `curl https://api.cc2asn.com/IPV4/NO`

## whois (TCP port 43)

Host: `cc2asn.com`, port 43. The query is the record type and the country code: `no`, `ipv4 no`, `ipv6 no` or `all no`.

- `whois -h cc2asn.com 'ipv4 no'`
- `echo ipv4 no | nc cc2asn.com 43` (use netcat if your whois client cuts long answers short)

## Limits and behaviour

- Free, with no account and no key: 100 queries a day and 30 a minute per person.
- Only the latest day is served; dated paths answer 404.
- An unknown country code answers 404. A few territories have no registered networks and also answer 404.

## Terms

- AS number (ASN): the number of an autonomous system, a group of networks run under one routing policy, usually by an internet provider, a company or a university. A 16- or 32-bit integer, written plain (65551) or dotted (1.15).
- Prefix: a block of IP addresses, also called an IP range or IP block, in CIDR notation, for example 192.0.2.0/24.
- Country code: the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code the registry has on file for the holder, for example NO for Norway, SJ for Svalbard and Jan Mayen.
